product_one_liner.value: koppla provides collaborative construction-scheduling software for general contractors, general planners, project developers and architects to plan projects, identify delays and coordinate construction work.
product_one_liner.notes: The homepage names general contractors, general planners, project developers and architects as users of its scheduling solution; the product description says it helps project managers keep construction projects on schedule by identifying delays.

pricing_page.notes: This is the company’s public pricing page, which describes its price model and says pricing depends on the customer’s specific needs.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: The company trust-center logo wall is headed “reviewed and trusted by” and names both Max Bögl and Implenia. | named_customers.0: Max Bögl is named on koppla’s “reviewed and trusted by” logo wall. | named_customers.1: Implenia is named on koppla’s “reviewed and trusted by” logo wall.

employee_band.notes: The company about page reports 38 employees. That count falls within the 21-50 band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The company profile explicitly identifies the headquarters as Potsdam, Germany; the city is Potsdam. | hq_country: The company profile explicitly identifies koppla headquarters as Potsdam, Germany; the country is Germany.

founded_year.notes: The funding announcement states that koppla was founded in 2020, which supplies the requested year.

eng_blog.notes: The blog index lists construction-industry guidance, import how-tos, feature announcements and event-related material, rather than multiple engineer-authored posts about how the product is built. This fits the specified negative criterion.

public_docs.notes: The public help center presents several article collections, including collections with 7, 19, 11 and 9 articles, meeting the requirement for several public documentation articles.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The open-jobs page lists a Founders Associate role and a Senior Product Engineer role, with no AI, ML, data-science or other qualifying title.

model_provider.notes: The company describes an AI-assisted project-import feature and links to its security center, whose visible subprocessors are listed, but neither disclosure names an AI model or model provider. I therefore leave the provider unknown.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: The company trust center lists GDPR and ISO/IEC 27001 under Compliance. I included those named items from the requested set and excluded TISAX, which is outside it. | compliance_certs.0: The trust-center Compliance list explicitly names GDPR. | compliance_certs.1: The trust-center Compliance list explicitly names ISO/IEC 27001.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The cited funding profile labels the latest round “Seed VC - III.” Other databases use different stage labels for this round, so I use the stage wording from the source reporting the USD amount and mark confidence medium. | funding_date: The profile dates its latest funding round to May 19, 2025; the requested YYYY-MM value is 2025-05. | funding_amount_usd: The funding profile reports the latest round as $6.76 million, so the amount is 6,760,000 USD.

raised_18mo.notes: The latest round is dated May 19, 2025, which is later than the start of the 18-month window (May 9, 2025) and before November 9, 2026.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The current jobs page lists only a Founders Associate and a Senior Product Engineer; neither is an SDR, BDR or account executive role.

launched_6mo.notes: A company LinkedIn post dated October 6, 2026 says the critical-path feature is now available and describes its behavior. October falls within the six months before November 9, 2026.
